findings.evidence: `EpsilonEridani/Mathematics/LieAlgebra/Casimir.lean:68-72`: "We therefore do not build any form into `LieModule.casimir`: it takes two families `b` and `b'` … but it deserves the name \"Casimir\" only when the two families are dual with respect to an invariant form"; `def casimir (b b' : ι → L)` at line 105, applied at SpinDecomposition.lean:283 with `spinGen : Fin 3 → Module.End ℂ ℂ²`.
findings.fix: State in the module docstring that this is `Σᵢ Sᵢ²` for the su(2) generators `spinGen`, taken via the general `casimir` construction with `L` the whole of `Module.End ℂ ℂ²`, so the centrality lemmas of `Casimir.lean` do not apply and the commutation statements here are proved directly. While editing line 279, drop the derivation sentence ("It follows from `S² = 3/2 + (σ(1)·σ(2))/2` and the exchange identity …") — it describes the proof and is already in the module docstring.
findings.issue: Line 50 ("The total-spin Casimir of the pair is `LieModule.casimir ℂ _ _ spinGen spinGen`") and the docstring of `casimir_spinGen_eq` (line 279) call this object "the Casimir" without qualification, but here `L = Module.End ℂ ℂ²` (finrank 4) and `b = b' = spinGen` is a 3-element family, so it can never satisfy the duality/expansion hypotheses that the imported `Casimir.lean` says the name requires; a reader will wrongly expect `LieModule.commute_toEnd_casimir` to apply to it.

findings.evidence: `theorem commute_toEnd_spinSingletProj (X : Module.End ℂ ℂ²) : Commute (LieModule.toEnd ℂ _ (ℂ² ⊗[ℂ] ℂ²) X) spinSingletProj` (lines 264-265); the docstring names no hypothesis or quantifier.
findings.fix: E.g. "For every operator `X` on `ℂ²`, the pair action `X ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ X` commutes with the singlet projector, so the singlet channel is an invariant subspace — in particular under the total spin `X = spinGen i`." Same for the triplet, and for the Main-results entry at lines 63-64.
findings.issue: "The singlet channel is invariant under the action of the pair" (line 263) and the same wording for the triplet (line 271) never mention the variable `X`: the statements hold for *every* operator `X` on `ℂ²`, which is both stronger and more specific than the docstring, and "the action of the pair" misnames the action *on* the pair.

findings.evidence: PR description: "The spin space is `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)` rather than `Fin 2 → ℂ` because … the `Pi.addCommMonoid`/`Pi.addCommGroup` instance mismatch keeps `Module.End ℂ (V ⊗ V)` from being recognised as a ring"; no such note appears in lines 15-74 or elsewhere in the file, whereas the comparable bracket gotcha is documented at lines 256-259.
findings.fix: Add an `## Implementation notes` paragraph stating the reason, next to the existing note on `LieRing.ofAssociativeRing`.
findings.issue: The module docstring nowhere records why the spin space is `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)` rather than `Fin 2 → ℂ`; that rationale (the `Pi` instance mismatch blocking the ring structure on `Module.End ℂ (V ⊗ V)`, on which every `mul`/idempotent lemma in the file depends) exists only in the PR description, which the source does not carry.

summary: Both files have module docstrings and every public declaration is documented, with references and cross-references that check out. Three docstrings are less honest or less informative than the statements they head: the "total-spin Casimir" label hides that `spinGen` is not a dual basis of the `L` it is applied to, the `commute_toEnd_*` docs drop the quantifier over `X`, and the non-obvious choice of `EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)` is documented only in the PR description.
